transcript.text: Just had a new induction hob fitted, Beko. When I put my saucepan on it just flashes a U and doesn't heat. Is it faulty? It's brand new!!

It is unlikely to be faulty: on Beko induction hobs, a flashing “U” normally means the zone cannot detect a suitable pan, rather than a hob error. The pan needs a flat magnetic base and must be large enough for the selected zone; aluminium, copper and some stainless-steel pans will not work. Try a fridge magnet on the pan base and, if possible, try a different known induction-compatible pan on the same zone. If a magnetic, flat, correctly sized pan gives “U” on every zone, contact the installer or Beko while it is new, as that would point to a hob or installation issue.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
I tried a magnet and it doesn't stick to the saucepans, but it does stick to my cast-iron casserole, and that one heated up fine. So is it just my pans?

Yes — it is the saucepans, not a fault with the hob. Because the magnet does not stick to their bases, they are not suitable for induction; the flashing U is the normal “no suitable pan detected” indication. Your cast-iron casserole heating normally suggests the hob can detect and heat compatible cookware. Look for pans marked “induction suitable”, or test the base with a magnet before buying: it should stick firmly and the base should be flat. Stainless-steel pans can be suitable, but only if they have a magnetic induction base.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

candidates: Pan not detected or unsuitable cookware (high)

reading.symptom: flashes U and does not heat when a saucepan is placed on it

plan: They asked: "Is it faulty?" - answer that first.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Beko; code U.
The fault they reported is: "flashes U and does not heat when a saucepan is placed on it". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

Explain what the error code means using ERROR CODES. If ERROR CODES does not resolve it, say plainly that you cannot confirm what it means on their model (it may not be an error code at all, for example part of the model name), never guess a meaning, and work from the symptoms.
They asked: "So is it just my pans?" - answer that first.
Already told them (do not repeat any of it; build on it): turn 1: gives check.

Checks they have done and what they found: Tested saucepans with a magnet - Magnet did not stick; Tested cast-iron casserole with a magnet and used it on the hob - Magnet stuck and the casserole heated up fine.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Beko; code U.
The fault they reported is: "flashes U and does not heat when a saucepan is placed on it". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 2: the checks they reported did not fix it. Give the next check that best separates the remaining likely causes, or say what the likely faulty part is if the checks already point to one. Until a check has confirmed which part has failed, name it as the likely part and the check that would confirm it; do not tell them to buy, order or replace it.
